title: Goldfish Survive 5 Months With No Oxygen by Brewing Their Own Alcohol

scenes.text: A pond freezes over. The goldfish inside get drunk.
Under the ice, the oxygen runs out for months. Almost any other fish would suffocate.
Goldfish and their wild cousin, the crucian carp, switch to a second set of enzymes that no other vertebrate has.
They turn the lactic acid that would poison them into alcohol, and breathe it out through their gills.
Their blood alcohol climbs past 50 milligrams per 100 millilitres, over the drink-drive limit in parts of Europe.
Up to five months, no oxygen, legally drunk. Then the ice melts, and they sober up.

description:
Goldfish and crucian carp can survive up to five months in oxygen-free water under ice by turning lactic acid into alcohol and releasing it through their gills.
A 2017 study by the University of Oslo and the University of Liverpool found their blood alcohol can pass 50 mg per 100 ml, above the drink-drive limit in some northern European countries, thanks to a duplicated set of enzymes about 8 million years old.
What other pet has a secret superpower?
subject: goldfish
first_comment: The trick comes from a whole genome duplication about 8 million years ago. Would you keep a pet that can out-drink you?
